topic: Geometric Foundations of Linear Algebra: From Systems to Spaces

sections.title: Geometric Interpretation of Linear Systems
sections.content: Introduce Ax=b as the intersection of hyperplanes. Visualize the system as constraints in space. Prerequisite: Basic understanding of vectors as coordinate points.
sections.example: A robot arm with two joints: each linear equation represents a constraint on an angle; their intersection is the specific pose of the arm.

sections.title: The Inverse Matrix: Unpacking the Transformation
sections.content: View the matrix A as a transformation grid. The inverse A⁻¹ is the 'undo' button. Explain that if a system is flattened (determinant 0), it cannot be undone.
sections.example: A photo-editing tool: Matrix A scales and rotates an image; A⁻¹ acts as the 'Reset' button that returns pixels to their original coordinates.

sections.title: Column Space: The 'Reachable' World
sections.content: Define Column Space as the span of the columns of A. Visually, it is the set of all possible output vectors b that the transformation can 'land on'.
sections.example: A cat moving in a 2D room: If the cat can only move along a specific diagonal plank, the column space is just that 1D line, regardless of how large the room is.

sections.title: Null Space: The 'Hidden' Kernel
sections.content: Define Null Space as the set of vectors x where Ax = 0. Visually, these are the directions that get 'squashed' into the origin.
sections.example: A security camera projection: Any movement of a person along the line of sight of the lens results in no change in the image (the projection is 0); that line of sight is the Null Space.

sections.title: Synthesizing the Big Picture
sections.content: Connect the concepts: If the Null Space contains only the zero vector, the transformation is invertible, and every point is reachable.
sections.example: A 3D printer: The 'Column Space' is the printable volume; the 'Null Space' represents design flaws where multiple distinct parts compress into the same coordinate, causing print failure.
